text.tspan: A calendar gives plans a place in time.
When we make a realistic plan, a little care can make the experience better. Planning and thinking about
First, reviewing a specific experience teaches more than a vague judgement. For example, we describe
one habit that helped us instead of calling the whole year good or bad. This is a small thing that makes
Second, a small next step is easier to act on than a broad promise. For example, we choose a
ten-minute practice session and put it on the calendar. We do not need a perfect day to do this well.
We can make a realistic plan more easily when we prepare and notice other people. These simple steps
give us a useful place to start.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Tell a friend. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are that reviewing a
specific experience teaches more than a vague judgement and that a small next step is easier to act on than a broad
promise. One example is that we describe one habit that helped us instead of calling the whole year good or bad.)
